Sōracte (Sauracte ), is, n. Sanscr. svar, heaven; cf.: serenus, 2. Soranus,
I.a high mountain in Etruria, on which was a temple of Apollo, now Monte S. Oreste, Varr. R. R. 2, 3, 3; Plin. 2, 93, 95, § 207; Hor. C. 1, 9, 2; Verg. A. 7, 696; 11, 785; Sil. 7, 662; 8, 494 al.—Masc. collat. form: “ad montem Soractem,” Plin. 7, 2, 2, § 19 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
